title: Sold Transaction
description: Ground-truth record of a completed sale for an asset, sourced from auction results, dealer-reported sold data, or an Atlas-facilitated exit. This is the training label for the AI Valuation Engine: listings are signals, sold transactions are truth. Every sold_transaction should resolve back to the listing (or listings, if the same asset was seen on multiple platforms) that preceded it via listing_record_id / dedup_key.

listing_record_id.description: FK to the listing record this sale closes out, if one was captured pre-sale. Null for sold comps ingested directly from auction-house results feeds with no prior listing crawl.

dedup_key.description: Same fuzzy-match key used on listing records, for linking sold comps across platforms.

origin.description: atlas_facilitated means Atlas itself brokered the purchase and/or resale; these are the highest-trust labels and also feed training_labels for the Buy Score model.

market_event_ref.description: FK to a market_event record explaining why this sale happened at this price (e.g. bankruptcy_auction, government_liquidation) — see market_event.schema.json. Mirrors listing.source.market_event_ref; null when no detected event applies.

identity_ref.description: FK to asset_identity.identity_id once VIN/PIN/serial decoding has run — mirrors listing.asset.identity_ref, letting the same physical unit's identity resolve across both its listing and sale records.

sold_price_usd.description: Normalized at time of ingestion using that day's FX rate; keep original sold_price/currency alongside it.

auction_type.description: Only meaningful when sale_type = auction_hammer. Unreserved auctions clear same-day at forced-liquidation pricing; reserved auctions mitigate downside via a target reserve.

valuation_basis.description: Which liquidation-value basis this sale represents. Typical mapping (see schemas/README.md): unreserved auction -> flv, reserved auction -> nflv, dealer_retail -> olv, wholesale -> nolv. Independently settable per record rather than hard-derived from sale_type/auction_type, since real transactions have edge cases.

last_asking_price.description: Final list/reserve/buy-now price immediately before sale, for computing sold-vs-asked spread.

days_on_market.description: From first_seen_at on the originating listing to sold_at.

atlas_outcome.description: Populated only when source.origin = atlas_facilitated. Realized economics of an Atlas-brokered buy-and-resell, distinct from the market sale price above when this record represents the resale leg.

opportunity_id.description: FK to the Opportunity Engine recommendation that led to this transaction.
